question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S={S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.12$ | $0.28$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.2$ | $0.18$ | $0.12$ |

Which of the following gives the covariance of $X$ and $Y?$
question.worked_solution:
The covariance of two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S$ is defined as

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y).
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.12$ | $0.28$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.2$ | $0.18$ | $0.12$ | $0.5$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.3$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $1$ |

We now compute $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =2\cdot 0.5+4\cdot 0.5 \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3 \\ \text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =1\cdot 0.3+3\cdot 0.3+5\cdot 0.4 \\  & =0.3+0.9+2 \\  & =3.2\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y) \\  & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-3)(y-3.2)f(x,y).\end{aligned}
$$
